# Use a stable, common base image suitable for CPU workloads.
# Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern toolchain.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend to avoid prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set a working directory for the application data.
WORKDIR /app

# Combine dependency installation, source code cloning, application build,
# and cleanup into a single RUN layer to minimize image size.
RUN \
    # 1. Install build dependencies and runtime requirements.
    # Includes compilers, CMake, Git, OpenMPI, and ca-certificates.
    # FIX: Added python3, which is a required dependency for the LAMMPS cmake configuration step.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    python3 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    #
    # 2. Clone the latest version of the LAMMPS source code into a temporary directory.
    && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /tmp/lammps \
    #
    # 3. Copy the required example files into the designated WORKDIR as per instructions.
    && cp /tmp/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ \
    #
    # 4. Create a build directory and configure the LAMMPS build.
    # We enable the specific REAXFF package and MPI support for parallel runs.
    && cd /tmp/lammps \
    && mkdir build && cd build \
    && cmake ../cmake \
    -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
    -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
    -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    #
    # 5. Compile and install the application.
    # Using -j$(nproc) speeds up the build by using all available CPU cores.
    # 'make install' places the 'lmp' executable in /usr/local/bin, which is on the system PATH.
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    #
    # 6. Clean up the source code and build artifacts to keep the final image lean.
    && rm -rf /tmp/lammps

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running as root and avoiding shared memory
# conflicts that can occur within Docker/Kubernetes cgroup limitations.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# Set the final working directory for the container's entrypoint.
WORKDIR /app

# The 'lmp' executable is now on the PATH.
# Provide a default command to facilitate interactive sessions.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS ReaxFF simulation,
# a typical High-Performance Computing (HPC) workload, using the Flux Operator
# on a Kubernetes cluster with AWS CPU instances.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deployed to the 'default' namespace as per instructions.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster's Indexed Job.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  # This can be more than the size (number of pods).
  # Flux will schedule these tasks across the available pods/slots.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines the container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend this with `flux run -n <tasks> ...`.
      # Note: We use the full path to the executable as provided in the instructions.
      command: /lammps/build/lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # The working directory is set to the location of the LAMMPS example input file
      # within the container, allowing the command to find `./in.reaxff.hns`.
      workingDir: /lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS

      # This is a worker container, not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

  # Job completion and cleanup policies.
  # Do not delete pods upon job completion to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected and optimized based on the failure analysis.
# It targets a specific ARM-based AWS instance for performance and uses the correct
# paths for the executable and working directory within the container.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster's Indexed Job.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # OPTIMIZATION: Increased tasks to 64 to fully utilize the vCPUs of the
  # selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance, aiming to minimize simulation wall time.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete pods upon job completion for debugging purposes.
  cleanup: false

  # Pod spec to select a compute-optimized instance for performance.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Flux spec to override the flux runner image for the ARM64 architecture
  # of the selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax

      # FIX: Corrected the command to call 'lmp' from the system PATH.
      # The executable is installed to /usr/local/bin/, not /lammps/build/lmp.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # FIX: Set launcher to true. The primary application container is the launcher.
      launcher: true

      # FIX: Corrected the working directory to '/app', where the Dockerfile
      # places the input files.
      workingDir: /app

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

updates.reason: The previous 19s runtime on a 64-core Graviton3 instance is a strong baseline. This attempt will test a different architecture, a 64-core Intel Ice Lake instance (c6i.16xlarge), to determine if its AVX-512 capabilities can provide a performance improvement for this LAMMPS workload.

The previous runs on 64-core Graviton3 (19s) and Intel Ice Lake (18s) were very close. This attempt will test a comparable 64-core AMD EPYC instance (c6a.16xlarge) to determine if it offers a performance advantage for this LAMMPS workload.

Previous tests on 64 vCPU instances (Intel, AMD, ARM) have plateaued at 18-19 seconds with 64 MPI tasks. This attempt will test if running one task per physical core is more efficient due to reduced cache contention. We will rerun on the c6i.16xlarge (32 physical cores), but reduce the task count from 64 to 32.

Performance has plateaued at 18 seconds. We have tested 64-core instances from all three major architectures (Intel, AMD, ARM) and found Intel/AMD to be slightly superior. A further test reducing MPI tasks from 64 to 32 on the best-performing Intel instance yielded no improvement, indicating we have reached the scaling limit for this problem size on this class of hardware. Further iterations are unlikely to yield significant improvements.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: true
    workingDir: /app
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c6i.16xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 32
